input.quote: For a renewable one-year term commencing upon the Maintenance Commencement Date, subject to payment of maintenance fees in accordance with the Fee Schedule but without additional fees or charges, Garman shall provide the following Maintenance Services:
input.rationale: Maintenance runs on a "renewable one-year term" (p0065) with no automatic-renewal mechanic, no non-renewal notice window and no multi-year roll-over, so renewal effectively requires the parties' agreement — the preferred position ("renewal only by mutual written agreement"). Exit is also unconstrained: the licence continues perpetually while fees are paid (p0117) and Sparkling may terminate at any time on 90 days' notice (p0118), so there is no notice-window or lock-in risk of the kind this rule targets. On pricing, fees are fixed by the Fee Schedule and Garman has no unilateral uplift right anywhere in the document (no "increase"/escalation language), so uncapped renewal repricing is not available to it. The absence of an express CPI/3% cap and of a 60-day vendor renewal reminder are preferred-only sub-elements that we note but do not redline, particularly as any fee change would require a written amendment. No deviation; nothing to propose.
